content:
Hi!

I think the new live.lean-lang.org Verso integration is really cool and a nice way to quickly test out Verso! Thanks for making it :heart:

I have been trying out IntegralApprox.lean and am wondering how to turn it into a local Verso project that builds the same web page?

I tried to look for a template on GitHub but found nothing (I searched for IntegralApprox.lean using GitHub's search). I tried to dig deeper and found Main.lean and VersoDemo.lean from live.lean-lang.org/api, but couldn't find where these files are on GitHub (again, I tried GitHub's search). I also couldn't find the lakefile from the API.

I already know how to set up a new Verso project, so my question is whether it's possible to do it more directly via live.lean-lang.org (by e.g. downloading a ZIP archive etc.)? This would, in my opinion, make it a bit easier to get started with Verso.

Another separate issue I noticed (which should arguably go into its own thread): when clicking go-to-definition on a name from Verso, live.lean-lang.org suggests to open https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/src/verso-manual/VersoManual/Basic.html for example, but the link goes a 404 page. Sorry if this is a known issue as I didn't check if somebody mentioned this already.

Aah, thank you for asking! Doc links not working are a known issue that I need to figure out a solution for. Let me get you a detailed step-by-step, but in the meantime, the short answer is that you want to follow the pattern of the project at https://github.com/leanprover/verso-templates/tree/main/basic-book , replacing Book.lean with your file.

Slightly improved answer: I've created an even more specific template at https://github.com/robsimmons/verso-templates/tree/basic-note/basic-note

It's very similar to the book example, mostly I convinced myself that my previous answer was pretty close to what I wanted to communicate.
